statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 13% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

Stress holds at 71% this hour rather than ticking higher, and the hold is a decision rather than an oversight. The Lebanon front did not add a new strike round in the last hour: the 08:29 IDT confirmation that the IDF killed Hezbollah's Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din at Deir al-Zahrani, and Defence Minister Israel Katz's 07:23 IDT vow that "no account on any front will remain unsettled," were both already scored in the previous assessment. What is genuinely new is smaller and points in two directions. At about 06:31 UTC Iran executed Shahram Sadeghi, whom its judiciary described as having acted "in support of the Zionist regime and the United States" - a hardening signal from Tehran with no equity transmission channel. At about 05:33 UTC Romania shot down a drone that breached its airspace near the Moldova border, intercepted by a Spanish NATO jet and the fourth such incident this year; a NATO-periphery recurrence, not a discontinuity. Against those, the Hormuz diplomatic channel reads constructively: the Iran-Oman shipping framework is awaiting final approval and Foreign Minister Araghchi calls a deal "very close," even as he conditions any actual reopening on US compensation and removal of the blockade.

New escalation and a live off-ramp roughly offset, so 71% is where the evidence leaves it. The discipline established last hour - a Stress point has to be bought by new evidence, not by the passage of another Sunday hour - is the reason this reads flat rather than continuing a climb.

Confidence holds at 70% (solid). Every cross-asset mark was re-verified from primary sources this hour and every one came back unchanged: NQ September 30,141.75, QQQ 731.07, VIX 14.25, 2Y 4.15% and 10Y 4.63%, WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52. The evidence is complete and fresh as evidence; it is the price leg that cannot be refreshed until the restart.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 13% maps to EA_ON for both instruments. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item this hour is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME Globex restart is the single checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window is anchored to it at 22:00-01:00 UTC (00:00-03:00 Berlin). Forecast Tail steps from 19% at 20:00 UTC to 20% at 21:00 UTC and 24% across the reopen, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) from 21:00 UTC through 03:00 UTC Monday before easing back to 19% and green. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment a whole weekend is priced at once: two rounds of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, an explicit Israeli vow to settle scores, a US naval blockade still shutting the Strait of Hormuz against an unsigned Iran-Oman framework - all against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it.

No US macro release lands inside the next 24 hours. Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first genuinely high-impact print. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and nothing here is a trade instruction.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 13% and status green; Stress deliberately flat at 71% as a new Iranian execution and a NATO-airspace drone downing are offset by an Iran-Oman Hormuz framework awaiting final approval - the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart remains the one checkpoint that matters
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first fifteen forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 70% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour and unchanged from the previous check. NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, day range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly marking the contract closed as of 14 August; the 52-week range is 22,961.50-30,975.50, putting NQ roughly 2.7% below its 52-week high. QQQ closed 731.07, -1.00 or -0.14%, day range 728.32-734.39 against a 555.60-748.65 52-week range, about 2.3% below the high, with a 730.85 after-hours print and "U.S. markets closed" on the page (Yahoo Finance). VIX 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, 52-week range 13.38-35.30, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42% on the day, about +5% on the week, +32.95% on the year) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation, both richer across the week from 4.25% and 4.72% on 10 August.

That set is internally conflicting, and conflict is a Stress input rather than a Tail input. Index futures are near - not at - 52-week highs, implied volatility is priced for calm on a 14 handle, duration is bid rather than offered, and only crude is expressing the geopolitical premium. Nothing in it is aligned into a one-way equity structure, and none of it can be aligned into one while the venue is shut.

What actually changed this hour, stated precisely. The Times of Israel liveblog carries three entries after the previous assessment's cutoff. At 08:33 IDT (about 05:33 UTC) Romania shot down a drone that breached its airspace near the Moldova border, intercepted by a Spanish NATO fighter and the fourth such incursion this year. At 09:17 IDT an explosive device damaged a south Tel Aviv apartment building in a suspected organised-crime attack with no injuries - not market-relevant. At 09:31 IDT (about 06:31 UTC) Iran executed Shahram Sadeghi, whom the judiciary said was "sentenced to death for having carried out an operational action in support of the Zionist regime and the United States." The two Lebanon items on the blog - the 08:29 IDT IDF confirmation of the Fakhr al-Din killing in the Badr regional division at Deir al-Zahrani, and Katz's 07:23 IDT statement that "no account on any front will remain unsettled" - were already scored in the 06:25 UTC assessment and are not double-counted here.

Why that produces a flat 71% rather than another tick. A NATO-periphery drone downing that has happened four times this year is a recurrence, not a discontinuity, and it has no observable Nasdaq transmission channel. An Iranian execution framed in anti-US and anti-Israel terms hardens Tehran's posture but moves no cash flow. Set against them, the Hormuz diplomatic read improved: the Iran-Oman framework - Iranian officials managing inbound traffic, Omani officials outbound, existing routes running temporarily before consolidation onto a central course - is awaiting final approval, Oman's foreign ministry calls the talks "positive and constructive," and Araghchi says the two sides are "very close." The offsetting caveat is explicit and load-bearing: Araghchi conditions any actual reopening on further terms including US compensation, and Iran's foreign ministry maintains that while the blockade stands "the necessary conditions for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz do not exist." Escalation with a live, named off-ramp is a different risk from escalation without one, and 71% is the honest reading of both halves.

The standing Hormuz configuration is otherwise unchanged: the strait effectively closed since late February, the US naval blockade reimposed after renewed attacks on commercial vessels, the IEA warning of the widest supply deficit in five years for 2026, and the June 17 Trump-Pezeshkian memorandum having already collapsed over which routes vessels may use. Two things cap how much of this belongs in Tail. Brent at $88.52 is far below the $126 March peak, so this market has absorbed a much larger version of the same shock and mean-reverted from it; and Hezbollah's promised retaliation remains undelivered, which is unresolved risk rather than realised transmission.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The next seven days contain no CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP or FOMC rate decision. Empire State and NAHB on Monday, Housing Starts and Building Permits Tuesday at 12:30 UTC with Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 13:15 UTC, the July FOMC minutes Wednesday at 18:00 UTC alongside a 20-year auction at 17:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and the S&P Global flash PMIs Friday at 13:45 UTC. Export and Import Prices did not appear on this hour's calendar read and has been dropped rather than carried forward on an unverified basis. Retail earnings dominate the corporate week - Home Depot Tuesday, Target, Lowe's, TJX and Analog Devices Wednesday, Walmart Thursday - so no megacap or semiconductor print capable of creating index-level one-way structure falls inside the window. The two largest scheduled catalysts sit just outside the seven days and are therefore correctly absent from the events array: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 report after the close on 26 August, against a consensus near $92bn revenue, and the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August with Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed Chair on the morning of 28 August. Those land roughly 36 hours apart and are the real shape of late August; they are not this window's problem.

Why Tail 13%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements and repeated extension. With no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe, and the last observed session was a quiet -0.15% drift inside a 254-point range. dominantMode stays mixed - conflicting cross-asset signals with no dominant direction.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 07:00 UTC Saturday to 06:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours, and the action was EA_ON, the status green and dominantMode mixed for all 24. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 13%. Stress is what moved: 48, 50, 51, 52, 53, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then 70 and 71. The first 22 of those are a near-monotonic 27-point climb across a market that never quoted once - each hour re-priced the same standing headlines slightly higher rather than re-testing them - and the 05:00 slot is the deliberate correction that stopped it, taken after re-verifying Friday's cross-asset marks against primary sources. The 06:00 slot then bought a single point with a genuinely new second round of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 70% as those marks were checked hour by hour, which is the part of the track that was earned. The rule now governing this series: a Stress point has to be bought by new evidence. This hour no new escalation round arrived, so no point was taken.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 06:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first eight hours after it are inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 14 of 24 slots, drifting 13% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 20% at 21:00 UTC and 24% across the reopen before easing through 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 04:00 UTC Monday. The forecast action is WATCH and the forecast status yellow from 21:00 UTC through 03:00 UTC. Stress rises gently from 71% to a 78% peak into the reopen - genuinely unpriced weekend risk does compound while the venue is shut, and this weekend carries an undelivered Hezbollah response on top of it - then eases to 72% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Confidence decays from 70% to 63% as Friday's marks age, then recovers to 73% after the restart, a larger recovery than the decay because a live price path is the single missing input. The last ten slots switch to event/whipsaw for a thin opening auction that has to absorb a full weekend at once. No US macro release falls inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first high-impact catalyst.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME Globex is shut and NQ has not quoted since Friday's 30,141.75 close, so there is no price path to score: no session direction, no gap, no retracement, no extension. Tail 13% is the correct floor for a market that cannot trend because it is not open. Stress holds at 71%.

Asian Sunday evening approaches with the venue still dark. The only live inputs are headlines. Nothing scheduled lands in this hour and the Lebanon front's next move belongs to Hezbollah, whose promised response is still undelivered.

Confidence begins its slow decay as Friday's marks age past 65 hours. The cross-asset set stays internally conflicting - NQ 2.7% below its 52-week high, VIX on a 14 handle, 2Y/10Y richer at 4.15%/4.63%, only crude carrying the geopolitical premium.
Tail ticks to 14% purely as unpriced weekend risk accumulates toward a single reopening auction. Still deep in the low band; still no observed directional efficiency to justify more.

Stress 72%. The Iran-Oman Hormuz framework awaiting final approval is a live off-ramp that caps how much of the energy premium belongs in equity Tail, but Araghchi's conditioning of any reopening on US compensation keeps the crisis unresolved.

Midday Sunday UTC. No US macro, no earnings, no central-bank speaker inside this hour. The next scheduled US datapoint is Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC; the week's first genuinely high-impact print is Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC.
